difficultyAxis: Top of tier 2: a text-shaped format rule (@Email) and a state-valued attribute, three stories and six scenarios, still create and read only. The child entity is created against a parent that may or may not exist.
rationale: The last blueprint before CRUD appears. It adds no new structural concept over tier2-02 but fills the tier 2 scenario budget and introduces a business-meaningful rejection (opening a ticket for an unknown customer) that is not a bean-validation failure. Update and delete are still absent, which is the visible tier 2/tier 3 boundary.

userStories.intent: register a customer with a contact email and a service tier
userStories.benefit: requests can be attributed to a known account

scenarios.given: a well-formed email address and a service tier
scenarios.then: the customer is persisted and returned with its generated identifier

scenarios.when: the agent attempts to register the customer
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid before reaching the service layer

userStories.intent: open a ticket for an existing customer
userStories.benefit: the request enters the support queue

scenarios.given: an existing customer identifier and a priority within the permitted range
scenarios.then: the ticket is persisted with its customer reference and opening time

scenarios.given: a customer identifier that does not exist
scenarios.when: the agent attempts to open the ticket
scenarios.then: the service reports the customer as not found

scenarios.given: a priority above the permitted maximum
scenarios.when: the agent attempts to open the ticket
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid

userStories.intent: read the tickets opened for one customer
userStories.benefit: the account history is visible before replying

scenarios.given: an existing customer with no open tickets
scenarios.when: the agent reads the tickets for that customer
scenarios.then: the service returns an empty collection rather than reporting an error
